biochem-metab-1:sites.q: Which pathway occurs in BOTH mitochondria and cytoplasm?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Heme synthesis, the urea cycle and gluconeogenesis all cross both compartments.

biochem-metab-1:sites.q: Why can a mature red blood cell not perform β-oxidation?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Without mitochondria the RBC depends entirely on glycolysis and can only make lactate from pyruvate.

biochem-metab-1:sites.q: A patient has a defect in the first and last enzymes of heme synthesis but normal intermediate steps. Where do those two enzymes act?
biochem-metab-1:sites.e: Heme synthesis starts and ends in mitochondria with the middle steps in cytosol, which is why defects can appear at either compartment.

biochem-metab-1:ratelim.q: The rate-determining enzyme of glycolysis is:
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: PFK-1, not hexokinase, is the committed and rate-limiting step.

o: Has no effect on either enzyme
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: One molecule flips both directions at once, so glycolysis and gluconeogenesis are never fast together.

biochem-metab-1:ratelim.q: A patient on a high-carbohydrate meal has high insulin. Which change best explains the fall in fatty acid oxidation?
o: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is inhibited by citrate
biochem-metab-1:ratelim.e: Insulin activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase, raising malonyl-CoA, which blocks fatty acid entry into mitochondria so synthesis and oxidation do not run together.

o: Electron transport in the respiratory chain
Transfer of acyl groups between enzymes
biochem-metab-1:carriers.e: NADH feeds the respiratory chain; NADPH drives biosynthesis and glutathione regeneration.
Also acetyl-CoA carboxylase and propionyl-CoA carboxylase. Biotin carries CO2.

biochem-metab-1:carriers.q: A malnourished man develops confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia. Which group of enzymes is impaired?
biochem-metab-1:carriers.e: Thiamine deficiency impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase and transketolase.

biochem-metab-1:glyco.q: The net yield of anaerobic glycolysis per glucose is:
biochem-metab-1:glyco.e: Four ATP are made but two are invested in the early steps.
Hexokinase/glucokinase, PFK-1 and pyruvate kinase are the three irreversible steps that gluconeogenesis must bypass.

biochem-metab-1:glyco.q: Arsenic poisoning allows glycolysis to continue but yields no ATP from the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate step. The reason is that arsenate:
o: Substitutes for phosphate, giving an unstable product
Blocks regeneration of NAD+ from NADH
biochem-metab-1:glyco.e: Arsenate replaces inorganic phosphate, so the high-energy acyl-phosphate never forms and the energy is lost as heat.

o: A higher Km and lower Vmax
A lower Km and lower Vmax
A higher Km and higher Vmax
The same kinetics but different tissue distribution
biochem-metab-1:hkgk.e: Low affinity, high capacity: the liver takes up glucose only when blood glucose is high.
It is the liver and beta-cell isoenzyme, raised after a meal.

biochem-metab-1:hkgk.q: A 19-year-old with mild, stable fasting hyperglycaemia since childhood has a strong autosomal dominant family history and no autoantibodies. A defect in which protein best explains this?
biochem-metab-1:hkgk.e: Glucokinase is the beta-cell glucose sensor; loss-of-function raises the threshold for insulin release, giving MODY rather than type 1 or type 2 diabetes.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Citrate inhibits PFK-1 because it signals that:
o: Energy and building blocks are plentiful
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: Citrate spilling out of a full TCA cycle slows glycolysis and promotes fatty acid synthesis.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Glucagon raises cAMP and activates protein kinase A in hepatocytes. The effect on the bifunctional PFK-2/FBPase-2 enzyme is to:
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: Phosphorylation switches off the kinase domain and switches on the phosphatase domain, so gluconeogenesis prevails.

biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.q: Which allosteric signal activates PFK-1 during vigorous exercise?
biochem-metab-1:glycoreg.e: A falling energy charge raises AMP, which accelerates glycolysis.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex requires all of the following EXCEPT:
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: Its five cofactors are TPP, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD and NAD+. Biotin belongs to the carboxylases.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: Arsenic inhibits lipoic acid. Which other enzyme is therefore also impaired?
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: It uses the identical set of five cofactors, so the two fail together.

biochem-metab-1:pdh.q: A neonate has severe lactic acidosis, poor feeding and neurological impairment; serum alanine and pyruvate are both raised. Which dietary change is most appropriate?
o: Increase fat and ketogenic amino acids
biochem-metab-1:pdh.e: In pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, pyruvate cannot enter the TCA cycle. A ketogenic diet supplies acetyl-CoA downstream of the block; more carbohydrate would worsen the lactate.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: In the Cori cycle, what travels from muscle to liver?
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: The liver reconverts it to glucose, which returns to muscle.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: The Cahill (glucose-alanine) cycle carries which additional substance to the liver?
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: Alanine delivers both a carbon skeleton for gluconeogenesis and nitrogen for the urea cycle.

biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.q: Pyruvate carboxylase is activated by acetyl-CoA. Physiologically this means that when acetyl-CoA accumulates, pyruvate is directed towards:
biochem-metab-1:pyrfate.e: A high acetyl-CoA signals that energy needs are met, so carbon is diverted to glucose synthesis instead of being burned.

biochem-metab-1:tca.q: Per acetyl-CoA, one turn of the TCA cycle produces:
Which enzyme belongs to both the TCA cycle and the electron transport chain?
biochem-metab-1:tca.e: It is complex II and the only TCA enzyme embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

biochem-metab-1:tca.q: TCA intermediates are constantly withdrawn for heme and amino acid synthesis. Which reaction best replenishes them?
biochem-metab-1:tca.e: Anaplerotic reactions refill the cycle; pyruvate carboxylase is the main one. The others move carbon within the cycle rather than adding to it.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: NADH yields more ATP than FADH2 because it:
o: Is oxidised faster by complex III
Carries two more electrons per molecule
Enters before an extra proton-pumping site
Binds directly to the ATP synthase
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: FADH2 enters via complex II and bypasses the first pump.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: Which complex contains copper and reduces oxygen to water?
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: Cytochrome oxidase. Its copper centres are required for the four-electron reduction of O2.

biochem-metab-1:etc.q: Energy from electron flow is used immediately to:
o: Pump protons across the inner membrane
Phosphorylate ADP directly at each complex
biochem-metab-1:etc.e: The proton gradient is the intermediate; ATP synthase then converts it into ATP.

biochem-metab-1:etcpois.q: Cyanide and carbon monoxide both act at:
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: They block cytochrome oxidase, halting electron flow and ATP synthesis together.

o: It inhibits the ATP/ADP translocase instead
It stops electron flow through the chain completely
It blocks complex I selectively and reversibly
It dissipates the gradient, speeding electron flow
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: DNP is a lipophilic proton carrier, so oxygen consumption rises but the energy is released as heat rather than ATP.

biochem-metab-1:etcpois.q: A man taking an illicit weight-loss drug presents with temperature 41 C, drenching sweat, tachycardia and a rising lactate; his oxygen consumption is high. Which effect explains his presentation?
biochem-metab-1:etcpois.e: Uncouplers such as 2,4-dinitrophenol let protons leak back, so substrate is burned fast and the energy appears as heat. An inhibitor would lower oxygen consumption instead.

biochem-metab-2:aa.q: Which two amino acids are purely ketogenic?
biochem-metab-2:aa.e: Both begin with L. Every other amino acid can contribute carbon to glucose.

biochem-metab-2:aa.q: Which amino acid is considered essential in growing children but not strictly in healthy adults?
biochem-metab-2:aa.e: Histidine and arginine are conditionally essential during growth.

biochem-metab-2:aa.q: During prolonged starvation, glucogenic amino acids are important because they supply:
o: Nitrogen for disposal by the urea cycle
biochem-metab-2:aa.e: Their carbon enters as pyruvate or TCA intermediates. Ketogenic amino acids cannot be converted to glucose.

biochem-metab-2:nh3.q: Which reaction actually releases free ammonia from amino acids?
biochem-metab-2:nh3.e: Transamination only funnels nitrogen into glutamate; deamination releases it.

biochem-metab-2:nh3.q: Ammonia is carried safely in the blood mainly as:
biochem-metab-2:nh3.e: Glutamine synthetase traps ammonia; it is the most abundant free amino acid in plasma.

biochem-metab-2:nh3.q: Why does hyperammonaemia affect the brain so severely?
o: The blood-brain barrier concentrates ammonia actively
The brain has no urea cycle and must trap ammonia as glutamine
biochem-metab-2:nh3.e: Brain detoxification depends on glutamine synthetase, and the process drains alpha-ketoglutarate from the TCA cycle.

biochem-metab-2:urea.q: The rate-determining enzyme of the urea cycle is:
biochem-metab-2:urea.e: It requires N-acetylglutamate as an obligatory allosteric activator.

biochem-metab-2:urea.q: Where do the two nitrogen atoms of urea come from?
biochem-metab-2:urea.e: The first enters via CPS I, the second is donated by aspartate in the argininosuccinate synthetase step.

biochem-metab-2:urea.q: A patient eats a very high-protein meal. Which change allows the urea cycle to accelerate appropriately?
o: Arginase is induced by dietary arginine
biochem-metab-2:urea.e: N-acetylglutamate is made from glutamate and acetyl-CoA, so it rises with protein intake and matches urea output to the nitrogen load.

o: Binding ammonia directly in the bloodstream
Inducing the hepatic urea cycle enzymes
Acidifying the gut so ammonia is trapped
biochem-metab-2:hyperam.e: The charged ammonium ion cannot be reabsorbed and is lost in stool.

biochem-metab-2:hyperam.q: Which drug lowers ammonia by reducing gut bacteria that generate it?
biochem-metab-2:hyperam.e: It is a poorly absorbed antibiotic used alongside lactulose.

biochem-metab-2:hyperam.q: A neonate is lethargic and tachypnoeic on day 3. Ammonia is 450 micromol/L, and arterial pH and anion gap are both normal. Which group of disorders is most likely?
biochem-metab-2:hyperam.e: High ammonia with a normal pH points to the urea cycle. Organic acidaemias raise ammonia too, but with a wide anion gap metabolic acidosis.

biochem-metab-2:otc.e: It is the only X-linked urea cycle disorder and the most common of the group.

biochem-metab-2:otc.q: Orotic acid appears in the urine in OTC deficiency because:
o: Carbamoyl phosphate is diverted into pyrimidine synthesis
Orotate is a normal end product of the urea cycle
Ammonia is converted to orotate by the kidney
Arginine is degraded to orotate in the liver
biochem-metab-2:otc.e: Carbamoyl phosphate spills from mitochondria into the cytosol and feeds the pyrimidine pathway.

biochem-metab-2:otc.q: A boy has orotic aciduria. Which finding distinguishes OTC deficiency from hereditary orotic aciduria?
biochem-metab-2:otc.e: Lippincott makes this the key discriminator: ammonia is high in OTC deficiency and normal in hereditary orotic aciduria, which instead has a megaloblastic anaemia unresponsive to B12 and folate.

biochem-metab-2:aader.q: Tetrahydrobiopterin is required for the synthesis of:
biochem-metab-2:aader.e: It is the cofactor for phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan hydroxylases.

biochem-metab-2:aader.q: Which amino acid is the precursor of both serotonin and niacin?
biochem-metab-2:aader.e: Diverting it toward serotonin can leave too little for niacin, producing pellagra-like features.

biochem-metab-2:aader.q: A patient with carcinoid syndrome develops dermatitis, diarrhoea and confusion. The mechanism is:
o: Histidine is excessively decarboxylated to histamine
Tryptophan is diverted away from niacin synthesis
Glycine is consumed by porphyrin synthesis
Tyrosine is shunted into melanin synthesis instead
biochem-metab-2:aader.e: The tumour consumes tryptophan, so NAD+ synthesis falls and a pellagra-like picture appears.

biochem-metab-2:pku.q: The enzyme deficient in classic phenylketonuria is:
biochem-metab-2:pku.e: Phenylalanine can no longer be converted to tyrosine, so tyrosine becomes essential.

biochem-metab-2:pku.q: Why must tyrosine be supplemented in PKU?
o: It is destroyed by the phenylketones
It can no longer be made from phenylalanine
It is not absorbed from the gut
It is lost excessively in the urine
biochem-metab-2:pku.e: Tyrosine becomes a conditionally essential amino acid in these patients.

biochem-metab-2:pku.q: An infant with high phenylalanine does not improve despite strict dietary restriction, and develops a movement disorder. Which explanation fits best?
o: Poor dietary adherence by the family
biochem-metab-2:pku.e: BH4 is also needed for tyrosine and tryptophan hydroxylases, so dopamine and serotonin synthesis fail. Diet alone cannot fix this; BH4 and neurotransmitter precursors are required.

biochem-metab-2:tyr.q: The urine of a patient with alkaptonuria darkens on standing because of:
biochem-metab-2:tyr.e: Homogentisate oxidase is deficient, so homogentisic acid accumulates and oxidises on exposure to air.

biochem-metab-2:tyr.q: Ochronosis in alkaptonuria refers to pigment deposition in:
biochem-metab-2:tyr.e: It produces dark ears and sclerae and early degenerative arthritis.

biochem-metab-2:tyr.q: Albinism increases skin cancer risk mainly because:
o: Melanin that absorbs ultraviolet light is missing
Immune surveillance of skin is impaired
DNA repair enzymes are also defective
biochem-metab-2:tyr.e: The defect is in tyrosinase or tyrosine transport, so melanin cannot be made. DNA repair is normal, unlike in xeroderma pigmentosum.

biochem-metab-2:msud.q: Maple syrup urine disease is caused by deficiency of:
biochem-metab-2:msud.e: Isoleucine, leucine and valine and their ketoacids accumulate.

biochem-metab-2:msud.q: Which vitamin is the cofactor of the enzyme deficient in MSUD?
biochem-metab-2:msud.e: The complex uses thiamine pyrophosphate, as do pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

biochem-metab-2:msud.q: Which branched-chain amino acid is most responsible for the neurological damage in MSUD?
biochem-metab-2:msud.e: Leucine and its ketoacid are the most neurotoxic, so dietary management restricts leucine most tightly.

biochem-metab-2:hcy.q: The commonest cause of homocystinuria is deficiency of:
biochem-metab-2:hcy.e: Homocysteine and methionine rise while cysteine falls.

biochem-metab-2:hcy.q: Which amino acid becomes essential in cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency?
biochem-metab-2:hcy.e: Cysteine is normally made from methionine via homocysteine, and that route is blocked.

biochem-metab-2:hcy.q: A tall thin 14-year-old has downward lens dislocation, a thrombotic stroke and intellectual disability. Which feature best separates this from Marfan syndrome?
o: The presence of a marked scoliosis
The tall stature with long thin limbs
The lens dislocates downward, with thrombosis
biochem-metab-2:hcy.e: Homocystinuria dislocates the lens downward and inward and causes thrombosis; Marfan dislocates upward and outward with no thrombotic tendency.

biochem-metab-2:cystin.q: The defect in cystinuria is in:
o: A transporter in kidney and intestine
An enzyme of the hepatic urea cycle
biochem-metab-2:cystin.e: It affects cystine, ornithine, arginine and lysine, which share one transporter.

biochem-metab-2:cystin.q: Which crystals are characteristic in the urine?
biochem-metab-2:cystin.e: Hexagonal cystine crystals are nearly diagnostic.

biochem-metab-2:cystin.q: Despite losing four amino acids in the urine, patients with cystinuria have symptoms only from stones. Why?
o: Only cystine is actually lost in the urine
The urinary losses are far too small to matter
The liver can synthesise all four of them
Peptide absorption still supplies those amino acids
biochem-metab-2:cystin.e: Di- and tripeptide transporters are intact, so nutritional deficiency does not develop; only the poorly soluble cystine precipitates.

biochem-metab-2:organic.q: Propionyl-CoA is produced from all of the following EXCEPT:
biochem-metab-2:organic.e: The sources are valine, odd-chain fatty acids, methionine, isoleucine and threonine. Leucine is purely ketogenic.
Propionyl-CoA carboxylase, the step before it, requires biotin instead.

biochem-metab-2:organic.q: A neonate has vomiting, lethargy, a wide anion gap metabolic acidosis and a mildly raised ammonia. Which feature points to an organic acidaemia rather than a urea cycle defect?
biochem-metab-2:organic.e: Urea cycle disorders raise ammonia with a normal pH, whereas organic acidaemias produce an acidosis with a wide anion gap.

biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.q: Which enzyme is absent from skeletal muscle, preventing it from releasing glucose?
biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.e: Muscle glycogen serves only the muscle; the liver and kidney have the phosphatase.

biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.q: Pyruvate carboxylase requires which cofactor and allosteric activator?
biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.e: Rising acetyl-CoA during fasting is the signal to divert pyruvate toward glucose.

biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.q: Why can even-chain fatty acids not be converted to glucose?
o: The pyruvate dehydrogenase step is irreversible
Fatty acids cannot cross into the liver
biochem-metab-3:gluconeo.e: Acetyl-CoA cannot be turned back into pyruvate. Glycerol and odd-chain fatty acids can make glucose because they enter past that block.

biochem-metab-3:hmp.q: The HMP shunt produces which two key products?
o: ATP and NADH for the chain
biochem-metab-3:hmp.e: It neither makes nor consumes ATP.

biochem-metab-3:hmp.q: Transketolase in the non-oxidative phase requires:
biochem-metab-3:hmp.e: Its activity is used as a laboratory measure of thiamine status.

biochem-metab-3:hmp.q: Beside reductive biosynthesis, NADPH is essential in neutrophils for:
biochem-metab-3:hmp.e: NADPH oxidase uses it to generate superoxide, which is why chronic granulomatous disease impairs killing.

biochem-metab-3:g6pd.e: It is common in Thailand and other historically malarious regions.

biochem-metab-3:g6pd.q: Which red cell finding is characteristic?
biochem-metab-3:g6pd.e: Oxidised haemoglobin precipitates as Heinz bodies, and the spleen removes them leaving bite cells.

biochem-metab-3:g6pd.q: A boy is tested for G6PD during an acute haemolytic episode and the level is reported as normal. What is the best explanation?
o: He must have a different enzyme defect
The most deficient cells have already lysed
The assay is unreliable during a fever
biochem-metab-3:g6pd.e: Reticulocytes have higher enzyme activity, so testing during haemolysis can be falsely normal. Repeat it weeks later.

biochem-metab-3:glycogen.q: The debranching enzyme has how many catalytic activities?
biochem-metab-3:glycogen.e: It transfers a three-residue chain and then hydrolyses the alpha-1,6 bond.

biochem-metab-3:glycogen.q: Branch points in glycogen are linked by:
biochem-metab-3:glycogen.e: The straight chains use alpha-1,4; branching every 8 to 12 residues allows rapid simultaneous degradation.

o: It allows storage without binding water
It protects glycogen from lysosomal enzymes
It makes the glycogen granule less soluble
It creates many ends to cleave at once
biochem-metab-3:glycogen.e: More non-reducing ends means glucose can be mobilised far faster during exercise or hypoglycaemia.

biochem-metab-3:gsd.q: Which glycogen storage disease is also a lysosomal storage disease?
biochem-metab-3:gsd.e: Acid maltase is the lysosomal alpha-1,4-glucosidase, so Pompe belongs to both groups.

biochem-metab-3:gsd.q: A child has exercise-induced cramps and dark urine but entirely normal blood glucose. Which enzyme is deficient?
biochem-metab-3:gsd.e: McArdle disease affects muscle only, which is why blood glucose is untouched.

biochem-metab-3:gsd.q: An infant has massive hepatomegaly, severe fasting hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricaemia and hyperlipidaemia. Which enzyme defect explains all of these at once?
biochem-metab-3:gsd.e: Von Gierke blocks the final shared step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, so glucose cannot leave the liver and the accumulating substrate spills into lactate, urate and lipid.

o: A benign condition, fructose in the urine
biochem-metab-3:fructose.e: Essential fructosuria is harmless because fructose is never trapped as a phosphate ester.

biochem-metab-3:fructose.q: Hereditary fructose intolerance is caused by deficiency of:
biochem-metab-3:fructose.e: Fructose-1-phosphate accumulates and sequesters inorganic phosphate.

biochem-metab-3:fructose.q: Why does hereditary fructose intolerance cause hypoglycaemia?
o: Trapped phosphate blocks hepatic glucose output
Aldolase B is also needed for glucose uptake
biochem-metab-3:fructose.e: Phosphate is sequestered in fructose-1-phosphate, so the liver cannot make or release glucose. Symptoms begin when fruit or sucrose is introduced.

biochem-metab-3:galactose.q: Isolated cataracts in an infant with no liver disease suggest deficiency of:
biochem-metab-3:galactose.e: Galactitol accumulates in the lens. Classic galactosaemia adds liver failure and intellectual disability.

biochem-metab-3:galactose.q: Classic galactosaemia results from deficiency of:
o: Galactokinase, the first enzyme of the path
Lactase in the intestinal brush border
biochem-metab-3:galactose.e: Symptoms begin with milk feeding, since lactose is the main dietary source.

biochem-metab-3:galactose.q: Infants with classic galactosaemia are particularly prone to sepsis with which organism?
biochem-metab-3:galactose.e: E. coli sepsis is a recognised and early complication of classic galactosaemia.

biochem-metab-3:sorbitol.q: Tissues damaged by the polyol pathway share which feature?
o: Both enzymes are present in excess
No glucose transporters in the membrane
Both of the polyol enzymes are absent
biochem-metab-3:sorbitol.e: Sorbitol is made but cannot be cleared, so it accumulates osmotically in lens, retina, kidney and nerve.
This also depletes the NADPH available for glutathione recycling, adding oxidative stress.

biochem-metab-3:sorbitol.q: The mechanism of cataract formation in galactosaemia is most similar to which diabetic complication?
biochem-metab-3:sorbitol.e: Galactitol and sorbitol are both trapped polyols that draw water into the lens.

biochem-metab-3:sphingo.q: Which finding distinguishes Tay-Sachs from Niemann-Pick disease?
biochem-metab-3:sphingo.e: Both have a cherry-red macula, but the spleen is spared in Tay-Sachs.

biochem-metab-3:sphingo.q: Which two lysosomal storage diseases are X-linked recessive?
biochem-metab-3:sphingo.e: All the others in these groups are autosomal recessive.

biochem-metab-3:sphingo.q: A man has episodic burning pain in his hands and feet, clusters of dark red skin papules, and progressive renal failure. Which enzyme is deficient?
biochem-metab-3:sphingo.e: Fabry disease: ceramide trihexoside accumulates in vascular endothelium, producing acroparaesthesia, angiokeratomas and renal and cardiac disease.

biochem-metab-3:muco.q: Which feature separates Hunter syndrome from Hurler syndrome?
biochem-metab-3:muco.e: Hurler clouds the cornea; Hunter does not, and Hunter is milder and X-linked.

biochem-metab-3:muco.q: Hurler syndrome is caused by deficiency of:
biochem-metab-3:muco.e: Hunter is due to iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency instead.

biochem-metab-3:muco.q: Mucopolysaccharidoses differ from sphingolipidoses mainly in that the stored material is:
biochem-metab-3:muco.e: Storing glycosaminoglycans affects bone, joints and connective tissue rather than mainly the nervous system.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ชายหนุ่มซึมหลังดื่มหนักและอดอาหาร
title.en: Boss case: Lactic acidosis after a binge and a fast

boss.case: A 24-year-old man is brought in confused after three days of heavy drinking with almost no food. He is tachypnoeic. Glucose 48 mg/dL, lactate 7.2 mmol/L, anion gap 22. He improves after thiamine, then glucose.

qs.q: Thiamine is given before glucose because thiamine pyrophosphate is required by:
o: Glycogen phosphorylase in liver and muscle
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the HMP shunt
qs.e: Giving glucose first drives pyruvate into a blocked complex, worsening lactic acidosis and risking Wernicke encephalopathy.

qs.q: His lactate is high mainly because pyruvate cannot:
qs.e: With pyruvate dehydrogenase impaired, pyruvate is shunted to lactate to regenerate NAD+.

qs.q: Ethanol metabolism raises the NADH/NAD+ ratio. This worsens hypoglycaemia by inhibiting:
qs.e: A high NADH/NAD+ ratio pushes oxaloacetate to malate and pyruvate to lactate, removing gluconeogenic substrate.

qs.q: Which enzyme is the rate-determining step of the pathway that his liver cannot run?
His glycogen stores are exhausted after three days. Which organ's glycogen could not have supported his blood glucose even when full?
qs.e: Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so its glycogen serves only the muscle itself.

qs.q: After recovery, which single deficiency would most closely reproduce his original biochemical picture?
qs.e: Thiamine deficiency impairs the same TPP-dependent dehydrogenases that caused his lactate to rise.
